(TRIVALENT) # MACHINING: 3.2 # WEIGHT(Kg ): 0.16 kg"}],"comment":"The material is left as a placeholder '#' in the title block and only vaguely specified as 'M.S.' (mild steel) in note N3, which does not identify a specific grade with known mechanical properties. This prevents procurement from sourcing the correct stock and makes it impossible to verify that the part has adequate strength or wear resistance for an adjuster plate. The designer should enter a specific material standard and grade (e.g., IS 2062 E250 or equivalent) in the title-block material field.","recommended_correction":"Replace the '#' in the title block material field and the generic 'M.S.' in note N3 with a specific, standardized material designation appropriate for the part's function."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"NOTE : (English) # MATERIAL: M.S. # FINISH: I.Z.B.P. (TRIVALENT) # MACHINING: 3.2 # WEIGHT(Kg ): 0.16 kg"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D6","page":1,"quote":"4"},{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D14","page":1,"quote":"34.5"}],"comment":"Note N3 specifies an I.Z.B.P. (trivalent zinc) plating finish, but the M5 threaded hole defined by dimensions D6 ('4') and D14 ('34.5') carries no instruction to allow for plating thickness on the thread. Plating buildup will reduce the effective minor diameter of the internal thread, potentially preventing the mating fastener from assembling. The designer should add a note specifying that threads are to be tapped oversize before plating or otherwise account for the coating thickness on the threaded feature.","recommended_correction":"Add a note indicating that the M5 thread must accommodate the I.Z.B.P. plating thickness, such as specifying an oversize tap drill or a pre-plate thread tolerance class."}]}
